sections.html:
Chili is a suburban town in the southwest corner of Monroe County, and its northeastern corner touches the city of Rochester. It covers about 39.9 square miles, almost all of it land. Downtown Rochester is roughly 7 miles northeast of the hamlet of Chili Center. Interstate 490 and the New York State Thruway both cross the town.

The town's own communities are Chili Center, North Chili, South Chili along the Thruway, West Chili near Black Creek Park, and the rural hamlet of Clifton.

Chili measureFigure
Total area39.85 square miles

Median age42.9 years

The population was up 1.7 percent from 28,625 in 2010. A median age of 42.9 and a household income of $89,793 point to settled families, and many sellers have owned for years.

Chili is split among several districts, so the one for your address depends on which part of town you live in. Churchville-Chili, Gates Chili and Wheatland-Chili central school districts all serve the town, and Caledonia-Mumford can apply to a parcel too. Your tax bill's school line settles which district applies, so check it before telling a buyer.

Route numbers get local names here. State Route 33A is Chili Avenue, State Route 386 is the Scottsville-Chili Road, and State Route 252 is Beaver Road. Town Hall is at 3333 Chili Avenue, and the Assessor and the Building Department work from the same building.

  • Interstate 490 is the main highway link toward Rochester.
  • The Thruway (Interstate 90) runs along the rural South Chili area.

sections.h2: How to challenge your Chili assessment
sections.html:
Every property in town is assessed at 100 percent of market value, using a July 1, 2024 valuation date for the current roll. The Assessor sets value and runs exemptions, while the school boards, the County Legislature and the Town Board set the tax rates.

The assessment calendar repeats each year, with these dates: exemption applications are due on the March 1 taxable status date, the tentative roll comes out May 1, Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May, and the final roll is filed July 1.

There are three levels of review, and each one wants evidence.

  • An informal review with the Assessor, by appointment from October through March, may include an inside and outside inspection.
  • A formal grievance goes to the five-resident Board of Assessment Review on form RP-524. The signed original must arrive with five copies, and faxed or emailed applications are not accepted.
  • Still unhappy after the board rules? File a small claims assessment review petition (RPTL-730) with the Monroe County Clerk, paying $30, no later than 30 days after the final roll.

Bring a recent appraisal, a purchase contract, comparable sales or photos of deferred maintenance. If you plan to sell, a signed listing or purchase offer is also the kind of document the board asks to see.

sections.h2: Property tax and the sale of a Chili house
sections.html:
In Chili, the Receiver of Taxes collects the town and county bill while each school district sends its own. Town and county bills are mailed at the very end of December and should arrive by the end of the first week of January. School bills go out at the very end of August and should arrive by the end of the first week of September. Homeowners with an escrow account get a receipt rather than a bill.

Paying by card at the Chili tax counter or on the town website carries a processing fee. Debit cards have a $3.95 minimum, and credit cards cost 2.45 percent with the same $3.95 minimum. Delinquent taxes owed to the County Treasurer are paid through the Monroe County website, so look at which office the bill names before you pay.

After a sale, the old bill belongs to the new owner. Return it to the Receiver with the new owner's name on it, or forward it directly. A new owner may also face an exemption recapture charge, a one-time amount the Assessor sets when the previous owner had an exemption the buyer does not qualify for. If you carry a senior or disability exemption, tell your buyer before closing so the charge is not a surprise.

sections.h2: Building Department and certificates of occupancy
sections.html:
The Building Department enforces the Chili town code and the New York building codes, and it issues certificates of occupancy or compliance after a final inspection. A project with a permit is not finished until that certificate is issued. Permit applications go through the CloudPermit online system, and the department answers questions about zoning and planning approvals.

Several town rules come up in resale talks.

  • Sheds from 1 to 119 square feet need no permit, sheds from 120 to 196 square feet need a building permit, and sheds of 197 square feet or more need a permit and a variance.
  • Fences need no permit unless the lot is in a flood zone or the fence sits in an easement.
  • Upgrading an electrical panel requires a building permit.
  • Domesticated farm animals, including chickens, need at least 5 acres.
  • The code enforcement officer responds to complaints about rubbish, litter, tall grass and unlicensed vehicles that can be seen from the public right of way.

Closing attorneys often request an instrument survey map. Look through your own closing papers first, then ask the Building Department whether one is on file, and try the Monroe County Clerk after that. If a past project never got a permit, the Building Department can tell you what closing it out takes.

sections.h2: Recording the deed at the Monroe County Clerk
sections.html:
Chili deeds are filed with the Monroe County Clerk, whose office is at 39 W. Main Street, downtown Rochester. A one-page deed costs $50, and every added page is $5. Filing the TP-584 transfer tax return costs $5, the RP-5217 equalization form costs $125 for residential property (and $250 for other property), and each residential deed carries another $10 fee.

The clerk charges transfer tax at $4 per thousand dollars of price. That matches the state rate of $2 for each $500, which the seller pays, and it is due with the TP-584 within 15 days after the deed is delivered. The buyer alone owes the state's 1 percent charge on residences priced at $1 million or more.

The deed must be a dated original with grantor and grantee addresses, a legal description naming the municipality, the new tax number, original signatures and a notary acknowledgment. For same-day recording, be in line by 4:30.

A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as is still goes through this same recording step, so your closing timeline depends on how complete your paperwork is, not on the buyer's financing.

faqs.q: What is the population of Chili, NY?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 29,123 people in the town of Chili, up 1.7 percent from 28,625 in 2010. Chili is a Monroe County suburb of Rochester.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Chili?
faqs.a: Every year, on the fourth Tuesday of May. Chili's Board of Assessment Review wants form RP-524 and your evidence in by 8 pm that day.

faqs.q: Which office collects property tax for a Chili house?
faqs.a: The Chili Receiver of Taxes collects the town and county bill at Town Hall, 3333 Chili Avenue. Delinquent taxes go to the Monroe County Treasury, and the school districts send their own bills in September.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell my Chili house?
faqs.a: The town issues a certificate of occupancy or compliance when permitted work passes its final inspection. Work done without a permit can be dealt with before listing if you ask the Building Department what it requires.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Monroe County?
faqs.a: Expect $50 for the first deed page and $5 for each more, plus the TP-584 ($5), the RP-5217 ($125 for a residence), a $10 residential fee and transfer tax at $4 per thousand dollars of price.
